item.title: The admin API, health and metrics
item.description:
Both are off unless the configuration asks for them, and neither is ever on the public listener.

admin {
 listen = "unix:///run/authn-bridge/admin.sock" # mode 0600
 # or over the network, mutual TLS and nothing less (loopback included):
 # listen = "10.0.0.5:9443"
 # tls_cert_file = "/etc/authn-bridge/admin.crt"
 # tls_key_file = "/etc/authn-bridge/admin.key"
 # client_ca_file = "/etc/authn-bridge/operators-ca.crt"
 # reflection = true # for grpcurl; off by default
}

metrics { listen = "127.0.0.1:9101" } # /healthz /readyz /metrics

disabled_file = "/var/lib/authn-bridge/disabled.json"

The listener is grpc-transports/control’s, shared with go-fileshare. The socket is never reachable by another user, not even between bind and chmod, and is never taken from an instance still running. TCP without all three TLS files is refused, loopback included, since every local user can reach 127.0.0.1:

authn-bridge: admin: control: listen address "127.0.0.1:9443" is TCP, which requires mutual TLS (loopback included: any local user can reach it); missing TLSCertFile, TLSKeyFile, ClientCAFile

A binary built with -tags nogrpc has no admin API, and refuses a configuration with an admin block rather than start without it.

The service

bridge.admin.v1.AdminService (proto/bridge/admin/v1/admin.proto), withgrpc.health.v1 beside it, which reports SERVING while the provider is ready.
Status version, issuer, start time; the federation’s metadata (IdPs, usable, valid until, last refresh, last error); what is held in memory
RefreshMetadata fetch the federation’s metadata now, and say how it went
ListIdPs the federation’s IdPs, as the institution list shows them (query, limit, 100 by default)
ListClients the configured relying parties
RevokePerson end their refresh token families, the access tokens those bought, their logins and device grants in progress and their application password, and revoke everything the certificate store holds for them: SSH and X.509 certificates (into the next KRL and CRL) and WireGuard keys
DisablePerson, EnablePerson refuse somebody here, at login and at every token, whatever their institution says, and revoke what they hold; optionally until a time
DisableIdP, EnableIdP the same for everybody one institution vouches for; a metadata refresh does not lift it
ListDisabled who is disabled, why, by whom, since and until when

Removing an IdP from saml { idps } ends what it vouched for, the wayDisableIdP does (from v0.23.7): a new login is refused, and so is every grant of someone who came through it, at the next use, with institution not configured: a refresh token (even across a restart), an application password,an SSH certificate request. Put the IdP back and they work again; nothing needs revoking.

With reflection = true, against a test provider:

$ grpcurl -plaintext -unix $PWD/run/admin.sock bridge.admin.v1.AdminService/Status
{
"version": "v0.23.4",
"issuer": "http://127.0.0.1:28473",
"started": "2026-10-26T11:22:17.441725Z",
"federation": {
"metadataUrl": "file:///tmp/authn/fed/metadata.xml",
"idps": 1,
"usable": 1,
"validUntil": "2026-11-02T11:22:16Z",
"lastRefresh": "2026-10-26T11:22:17.442875Z"
},
"counts": {}
}

Disabling 

$ grpcurl -plaintext -unix -d '{"username":"alice@univ-example.example","reason":"left the lab"}' $PWD/run/admin.sock bridge.admin.v1.AdminService/DisablePerson
{
"disabled": {
"username": "alice@univ-example.example",
"reason": "left the lab",
"by": "uid=501",
"since": "2026-10-26T11:22:17.952680Z"
},
"revoked": {}
}
$ grpcurl -plaintext -unix -d '{"entity_id":"https://idp.univ-example.example/idp/shibboleth","reason":"compromised","until":"2026-11-27T08:00:00Z"}' $PWD/run/admin.sock bridge.admin.v1.AdminService/DisableIdP
{
"disabled": {
"entityId": "https://idp.univ-example.example/idp/shibboleth",
"reason": "compromised",
"by": "uid=501",
"since": "2026-10-26T11:21:27.038956Z",
"until": "2026-11-27T08:00:00Z"
},
"revoked": {}
}

revoked counts what each call ended (refresh families, access tokens, logins,application passwords, certificates); nothing was live here. Every call that changes something is logged with who made it, the peer’s uid= on the socket or the client certificate’s cn= over TLS:

disabled alice@univ-example.example (0 known identities) by uid=501 until enabled again: left the lab
revoked alice@univ-example.example: 0 refresh families, 0 access tokens, 0 logins, 0 app passwords, 0 certificates
disabled IdP https://idp.univ-example.example/idp/shibboleth by uid=501 until 2026-11-27T08:00:00Z: compromised
revoked IdP https://idp.univ-example.example/idp/shibboleth: 0 refresh families, 0 access tokens, 0 logins, 0 app passwords, 0 certificates
enabled alice@univ-example.example by uid=501

A person is disabled as who they are. Usernames compare without case, as eppn, uid, mail and subject-id all do, so the same call with"Alice@Univ-Example.example" lifts what was set for alice@univ-example.example ({"wasDisabled": true}). The entry also records the stable identity of everybody known under that name, so another spelling from their IdP does not let them back in. A name with no @ is also matched as a sub, for a person whose IdP releases no username.

The entry is recorded before anything is revoked, so a grant racing the revocation meets the entry.

Names fold ASCII letters only (since v0.23.8). The disable list, the certificate principals and the subject-id compare usernames with go-authn/oidc’s ASCIILower, so a Kelvin sign (U+212A) is not a “k”: kate and its spelling with a Kelvin sign are two people, with two disable entries and two certificate principals. Disabling one does not disable the other.

Disabling is kept in disabled_file, and refused without one. Somebody disabled until the next restart would be let back in by the next deployment:

$ grpcurl -plaintext -unix -d '{"username":"alice@univ-example.example"}' $PWD/run/admin.sock bridge.admin.v1.AdminService/DisablePerson
ERROR:
Code: FailedPrecondition
Message: disabling needs disabled_file in the configuration: without it, a restart would forget who is disabled

A file that cannot be read stops the provider from starting, for the same reason. A disabled institution counts as not usable in Status, ListIdPs andcheck.

What disabling reaches beyond the provider is onrevocation: the KRL and the CRL for certificates, Shared Signals for tokens. An application password removed here stops working in go-fileshare when it next reads its directory;call its ReloadDirectory after DisablePerson for the effect to be immediate.

What RevokePerson cannot end

An access token already handed out is a signed statement a resource server checks on its own, valid there until it expires (an hour by default). An SSH certificate already issued lasts its validity unless the server reads the KRL, which is why both are short.

Passkey removal notices

With a mail block (since v0.32.0), a local account is told, at its own address, when a passkey removal is requested or cancelled, so that a thief holding one key cannot cancel the owner’s removal in silence. It concerns local accounts only, and the notice is one mail per account per window (default 10 minutes): the events that arrive meanwhile are collapsed into one digest. What an operator sees depends on the event:

  • A removal request whose notice cannot be sent stays pending. It is not carried out when its delay ends. The bridge retries (5 tries, with a growing pause), then logs GAVE UP loudly; a restart resumes it, and so does the next event. The key keeps working meanwhile, as before. The record carriesnotice_pending until a notice has been delivered.
  • A cancellation applies even if its mail fails. The failure is logged(mailing <login> failed) and shown on the account page, which says the notice could not be sent.
  • An account with no usable address is not blocked: its removal proceeds as without a mail block, the log says <login> has no usable mail address ... nobody is told, and the account page says so.

Without a mail block nothing changes.

The journal, and local accounts

Since v0.37.0 every successful sign-in leaves one line in the journal, and none of them holds a secret: no code, token, assertion, mail address, name or group.

login: <username> via <idp entityID> for <client_id> from <address>
login: <login> via <issuer>/local with passkey <8 hex> for <client_id> from <address>
account: <username> confirmed through <idp entityID> from <address>
account: audit: <login> stepup <16 hex> from <address>
token: authorization_code issued to <client_id> for <username>
token: refresh_token issued to <client_id> for <username>

The first two are a login at the authorization endpoint, through an institution and with a local passkey (<8 hex> is the passkey’s ID aslocal: <login> enrolled a passkey (<8 hex>) prints it). The next two are the account page’s sign-in, through an institution and with a passkey. The last two are the tokens handed to a client.

Run authn-bridge local-account … as root when the accounts directory isroot:authn-bridge 0750 and the file 0640, the documented layout: the command replaces the file through a temporary one next to it, and as authn-bridge it fails with open /etc/authn-bridge-local/.accounts-NNN: permission denied. It keeps the file’s owner and mode. Over SSH, ssh host sudo authn-bridge local-account … --name "Two words" needs an inner layer of quotes(--name '"Two words"'), because ssh joins its arguments into one string that the remote shell splits again.

Which accounts a client takes

Since v0.38.0 a client block may take one kind of person only:

client "forgejo" {
 secret_file = "/etc/authn-bridge/forgejo.secret"
 redirect_uris = ["https://git.example.org/user/oauth2/bridge/callback"]
 accounts = ["local"] # "local", "federated", or both (the default)
}

accounts = ["local"] is for a service that wants a hardware key: a person of a SAML institution is refused. The rule is held everywhere a grant is made or used, not only where a login is offered. The authorization endpoint sends the person to the one path the client takes (prompt=none for a local-only client answers login_required); the federation step, the passkey step and the end of a login each refuse a login of the other kind; the code exchange, a refresh and a device poll refuse a person of the other kind, so a grant bought before the restriction was written stops with it. The answer is access_denied, at the client’s redirect URI during a login and at the token endpoint afterwards.authn-bridge check prints the restriction on the client’s line, local needs a local block, and bridge_logins_total{result="wrong_account_kind"} counts the refusals. The journal says why:

login: <username> via <idp entityID> refused for <client_id>: this client takes local accounts only
token: account kind not accepted by this client: <why> (<username> via <idp> for <client_id>)

Known limit: the certificate endpoints (SSH, X.509, Kerberos, WireGuard) are not tied to a client, so accounts does not apply to them.

Administrators who invite from the web

Since v0.39.0 an administrator can invite a local account at /account/invite (login, e-mail address, optional name), without a shell on the host. It is the same invitation as the command line’s, and the link goes only by e-mail, to the invitee. The administrators are named in the local block, with the authenticator models they may use:

local {
 admins = ["alice"]
 admin_aaguids = ["9dd8d593-2213-438a-97f8-d6b813d51c27"]
 mds_dir = "/var/lib/authn-bridge/mds"
}

The page needs a mail block, a user-verifying assertion at most three minutes old, and a CSRF token; each administrator may invite ten accounts an hour. An administrator’s passkey model must be proved, not reported: registration asks the browser for a direct attestation, go-authn/webauthn v0.3.0 verifies it(a packed statement with an x5c chain; self and none verify but prove no model), and the model is checked against the FIDO MDS3 metadata, in go-authn/fido v0.16.0’s mds. Only then does the bridge record the model, and the page reads nothing else. A model the metadata later reports revoked or compromised stops opening the page. A key registered without a proven model still signs in; it opens nothing.

The metadata is kept in mds_dir, which is optional, defaults to/var/lib/authn-bridge/mds, must be an absolute path, and is refused withoutadmins. A background goroutine fetches it, never a request. The host needs:

  • a directory the service may write (mds_dir; another path than the default must be in the unit’s ReadWritePaths=);
  • outbound HTTPS to mds3.fidoalliance.org, and outbound plain HTTP to the CRL distribution points of its certificates;
  • a correct clock.

The service starts without the metadata and retries; until it is in, no administrator key is proved and the page refuses.

Registering an administrator’s key again. A key registered before v0.39.0 has no verified attestation. For each administrator: sign in with the existing key, open /account, confirm with the key, and add a passkey with the allowed authenticator (the YubiKey Bio, for example), accepting the browser’s prompt to share its make and model. The answer must say attested: true; then/account/invite works. Remove the old key afterwards.

Health and metrics

go-net-health/endpoint’s, as in go-fileshare, on the metrics listener, which must not be the public one (a configuration that makes it so is refused):
/healthz up while the process answers
/readyz ready while the federation’s metadata is loaded and within its validUntil, and no revocation is waiting to reach the state database
/metrics Prometheus text, bridge_* families 
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:28475/metrics | grep "^bridge_"
bridge_build_info{version="v0.23.4",goversion="go1.27.3",revision="6e0156cb516ace9091d4070c425258febc48f6ee"} 1
bridge_start_time_seconds 1793013737
bridge_ready 1
bridge_metadata_valid_until_timestamp_seconds 1793618536
bridge_metadata_idps 1
bridge_metadata_last_refresh_timestamp_seconds 1793013737
bridge_metadata_refreshes_total{result="failed"} 0
bridge_metadata_refreshes_total{result="ok"} 1
bridge_logins_in_progress 0
bridge_devices_waiting 0
bridge_refresh_families 0
bridge_access_tokens 0
bridge_disabled{kind="idp"} 0
bridge_disabled{kind="person"} 0
bridge_ssh_certificates_total 0
bridge_x509_certificates_total 0

The counters of logins by outcome (bridge_logins_total), of tokens by grant(bridge_tokens_issued_total) and of application passwords(bridge_app_passwords_total) appear only once they have counted something. No label names a person or an institution: which universities’ people use the service, and when, is not the provider’s to publish. Alert on bridge_metadata_valid_until_timestamp_seconds before the time it gives is reached: past it, nobody can log in.
